title: Despite AI hype, Google's data shows workers aren't automating themselves away
excerpt: Analysis of 15 million real AI interactions finds most tasks at most jobs are unaffected.
content_html:
The researchers also attempted to measure how deeply AI was being integrated into various jobs, looking at how often individual, granular O*NET work tasks were attempted using Gemini. Across that entire database, the ATLAS researchers only classified 21 percent of all work-related tasks as “Gemini tasks”—those that met a minimum threshold of 25 related interactions attempted in the massive sample.

For many occupations (29%), not a single relevant work task achieved this “non-negligible” Gemini usage threshold, suggesting those jobs have been minimally impacted by the AI revolution so far. For another 30 percent of all occupations, less than one-quarter of tracked tasks saw significant related Gemini usage, suggesting humans were still the ones responsible for the vast majority of the component parts of those jobs.

In only 3 percent of occupations was Gemini being regularly consulted for at least three-quarters of that job’s relevant tasks. Jobs like software quality assurance analysts and testers, human resources specialists, and document management specialists fell into this bucket and are seemingly the most impacted by AI use in the study.

Altogether, the researchers write, these kinds of numbers suggest that “AI is currently serving primarily as a complement to existing work” and that “AI appears useful for a subset of tasks performed within occupations, but they do not currently appear to be comprehensively used for performing the work currently done by humans.” While the researchers say that this state of affairs may change “as new AI breakthroughs emerge,” it’s also possible that new workflows “will maintain a degree of complementarity between workers and AI systems.”

Give AI the low-expertise, non-routine work

Beyond looking at high-level occupations, the Google researchers also looked at the specific kinds of work tasks that Gemini users ask the model to undertake. Cognitive tasks (i.e. those that primarily involve thinking) represented a whopping 86 percent of the Gemini interactions measured (by volume), while interpersonal and manual tasks were underrepresented in the sample compared to their workplace prevalence.

content_html_zh:
研究人员还试图衡量人工智能融入各种工作的深度，观察使用 Gemini 尝试单独、细粒度的 O*NET 工作任务的频率。 在整个数据库中，ATLAS 研究人员仅将所有与工作相关的任务中的 21% 归类为“双子座任务”，即在大量样本中满足 25 次相关交互尝试的最低阈值的任务。

对于许多职业（29%）来说，没有一项相关工作任务达到了这一“不可忽视的”双子座使用阈值，这表明迄今为止这些工作受到人工智能革命的影响很小。 对于另外 30% 的所有职业，只有不到四分之一的跟踪任务与 Gemini 的使用有显着相关，这表明人类仍然负责这些工作的绝大多数组成部分。

在只有 3% 的职业中，至少四分之三的相关任务会定期咨询双子座。 软件质量保证分析师和测试人员、人力资源专家和文档管理专家等工作都属于这一类，并且在研究中似乎受人工智能使用的影响最大。

研究人员写道，总而言之，这些数字表明“人工智能目前主要是作为现有工作的补充”，并且“人工智能似乎对职业中执行的一部分任务很有用，但它们目前似乎并未全面用于执行目前由人类完成的工作。” 尽管研究人员表示，“随着新的人工智能突破的出现”，这种状况可能会发生变化，但新的工作流程“也有可能在工作人员和人工智能系统之间保持一定程度的互补性”。

让人工智能承担低专业性、非常规的工作

除了研究高级职业之外，谷歌研究人员还研究了 Gemini 用户要求模型承担的具体工作任务类型。 认知任务（即主要涉及思考的任务）占双子座互动量的高达 86%（按数量计算），而与工作场所的普遍情况相比，人际任务和体力任务在样本中的代表性不足。
